submitted.rationale: Index 25 (Mn 0.49/Sr 0.51) had the highest measured photocurrent, 4.26 uA. This is the SrMnO3 region, which MEGNet predicts has the widest stable semiconducting gap in the system (hexagonal SrMnO3, ~1.8 eV HSE). Photocurrent peaked here and fell on both sides.

rejected.reason: Measured 0.07 uA. Sr7Mn4O15 is stable (gap 1.64 eV), but the photocurrent was far lower.
Measured 3.08 uA, below index 25. Sr3Mn4O12 is off the hull and has a smaller gap (1.09 eV).
Predicted gap is near-metallic (0.04 eV). SrMn2O6 has a large gap but is 0.21 eV/atom above the hull.

consultations.verdict: Support: hexagonal SrMnO3 (Mn 0.5) predicted HSE gap 1.79 eV, the largest semiconducting gap among the ternaries checked; SrMn7O12 (0.04 eV) and Sr2MnO4 (0.29 eV) are near-metallic. So Mn~0.5 (index 25) is the most promising region for photoresponse at 3.22 eV.

Support: Sr7Mn4O15 (Mn 0.364) is on the MACE hull (0.004 eV/atom), with a predicted gap of 1.64 eV, so it is a stable semiconducting phase that should form near index 16. SrMn2O6 has a large gap (2.78 eV) but sits 0.21 eV/atom above the hull, so it is unlikely to form. That argues against spending on the Mn~0.67 region.

Mixed/weak support: Sr3Mn4O12 (Mn 0.57) is 0.09 eV/atom above the MACE hull, and its predicted gap is 1.09 eV, smaller than SrMnO3's. Index 20 (Mn 0.566) will therefore likely be SrMnO3-dominated with a Mn-rich secondary phase. The data show photocurrent rising toward Mn~0.5 (4.3 uA at 0.49 vs 0.07 uA at 0.38), and the GP ranks index 20 highest by mean (2.9e-6, sd 3.2e-6). I'm using the last measurement to test the Mn-rich side of the SrMnO3 region.
